results.market_title: Will the highest temperature in Seoul (Incheon) be 27°C on September 1?
results.reasoning: Two days before the observation date, near-term aviation forecasts for RKSI (Incheon Airport) suggested daily max temperatures clustering around 28-29°C, somewhat above the September climatological average high near 25-26°C for Incheon. This makes 27°C a plausible but not clearly modal whole-degree bucket—28°C or 29°C appear at least as likely given the warm forecast trend, so 27°C likely captures a meaningful but not dominant share of the probability mass.
results.key_findings: ["AccuWeather September 2026 climate average high for Incheon is ~77°F (~25°C), with monthly range 72-84°F (22-29°C)","KMA aviation weather office (amo.kma.go.kr) snippet for RKSI showed forecast 'Max. Air Temp. 29°' repeated across multiple upcoming days, suggesting a warm spell heading into early September","No single authoritative day-specific (Sep 1) forecast in whole-degree Celsius was retrieved with full confidence due to search tool rate limits","Whole-degree-bucket temperature markets typically have a modal bucket probability in the 25-35% range given forecast uncertainty 2 days out"]

results.market_title: Will the highest temperature in Wellington be 14°C on September 1?
results.reasoning: AccuWeather's forecast (2 days out) puts Wellington's Sept 1 high near 59°F (~15°C), slightly above the 14°C threshold in question, though short-range forecast noise and the airport station's typically cooler/windier microclimate versus city readings leave meaningful uncertainty. With whole-degree bucket resolution, 14°C and 15°C both appear plausible, but current forecast data leans marginally toward 15°C as the more likely outcome.
results.key_findings: ["AccuWeather day-ahead forecast shows Sept 1 high of 59°F (~15.0°C) for Wellington","No detailed hourly/airport-specific forecast (MetService/NIWA) was found with finer granularity","Wellington Airport station often reads slightly cooler than city-center forecasts due to wind exposure","Short forecast horizon (2 days) increases reliability but single-degree bucket resolution still carries real uncertainty"]

results.market_title: Will MrBeast hit 139 billion views by August 31?
results.reasoning: Cross-referencing multiple third-party trackers (vidIQ, ChannelMetrics, VidMaestro, HypeAuditor subscriber counts) and extrapolating from a known June 27 (131.3B) to Aug 9 (136.35B) growth rate of ~117M views/day, MrBeast's channel is estimated to sit at roughly 138.6-138.8B total views as of Aug 29, 2026, needing about 300-400M more views in the ~2.5 days remaining until the Aug 31 11:59pm ET deadline — almost exactly matching his typical daily growth rate, making this a near coin-flip. A newly implemented YouTube policy (effective 8/24/2026) that counts views from the first frame rather than after ~30 seconds could modestly accelerate view accrual right in this window, providing some upside tilt, while data noise across trackers (ranging from 133.7B to 138.3B for supposedly 'current' figures) creates meaningful uncertainty in the true starting point.
results.key_findings: ["vidIQ shows MrBeast at 138,296,359,751 total views with 515M subscribers, gaining ~3.19B views in the trailing 28 days (~114M/day)","HypeAuditor confirms ~514.4M subscribers as the current August 2026 figure, corroborating vidIQ's recency","VidMaestro (updated Aug 9, 2026) showed 136.35B views/512M subs; extrapolating the implied ~117M views/day growth rate to Aug 29 lands at ~138.7B, just under the 139B threshold with ~2.5 days left","A YouTube-wide policy change effective 8/24/2026 counts views instantly from first-frame play (like TikTok/Instagram) rather than after ~30 seconds, which YouTube itself said would make 'total view counts move faster' — a tailwind for reaching the threshold in this exact window","A prior similar market ('hit 120B by April 30') resolved NO after landing at ~119.6B, showing these round-number thresholds have recently been narrowly missed"]

results.market_title: Kristi Noem divorce by August 31?
results.reasoning: Multiple credible outlets (Daily Mail, TMZ, Daily Beast, Yahoo/AP, Advocate) reported in mid-July 2026, sourced from Noem's own mother, that Kristi Noem intends to divorce husband Bryon Noem following the 'bimbofication' scandal, with a quote attributed to Noem via her mother: 'We're going to get a divorce.' No formal court filing or first-person statement from Noem or Bryon has surfaced, and some outlets explicitly note 'no divorce filing has been publicly reported' and Noem herself hasn't personally confirmed it, which creates ambiguity about whether this meets the bar of a direct announcement vs. 'definitive consensus of credible media reporting.' Given the breadth and consistency of the reporting (multiple independent outlets, direct quote, no denial found) occurring well before the Aug 31 deadline, there's a reasonable case for YES, but the low crowd price (14%) suggests market participants may be applying a stricter standard requiring a more direct/official announcement rather than a mother's secondhand account, so I weight this as roughly a coin-flip with an upward tilt from the evidence.
results.key_findings: ["Daily Mail (July 10, 2026) first reported, via Noem's mother, that Kristi Noem plans to divorce Bryon Noem after 34 years of marriage","Multiple outlets (TMZ, Daily Beast, Yahoo, Advocate, Gateway Pundit) republished the story with a quote attributed to Noem via her mother: 'We're going to get a divorce'","Several outlets caveat that 'no divorce filing has been publicly reported' and Noem has not personally issued a statement confirming the split","Noem's representatives reportedly asked for 'privacy and prayers for the family' rather than confirming or denying divorce plans","No search results found of a retraction, denial, or official confirmation as of the latest available information"]
